title: The hole in the record, and what the minutes filled
question: Which votes cannot be read from the Board’s vote pages, how many did the minutes supply, and which are still missing?
finding: For 332 roll calls on money files and lobbied measures the Clerk’s vote page announces a vote and names no member; 306 of them are dated 13 April 2016 to 26 July 2016. The Clerk’s published minutes of the same meetings supplied the names for 315, 278 of them on money files. That restores the final Board vote on 104 money files naming $3.43 billion in their titles: 98 passed with no dissent and 6 drew a no (file 160295, 8 to 3; file 160296, 8 to 3; file 160357, 10 to 1; file 160466, 10 to 1; file 160539, 10 to 1; file 160628, 10 to 1). 17 roll calls remain without member votes: 14 where the minutes also print no names, 2 where the minutes print the action twice with different votes, and 1 that the minutes do not print. 15 of the 17 are on money files, and for 14 of those the file’s final vote is on record all the same. 1 money file is left out of every count because its final passage is one of them: file 160358 (Appropriation and De-Appropriation - Surplus Revenue and Expenditures - Supporting Increased Overtime …): printed twice: 6 to 5 (noes: Avalos, Campos, Cohen, Kim, Peskin), then 7 to 4 (noes: Avalos, Campos, Kim, Peskin), so it passed over at least 4 noes whichever is the vote on record. Separately, 77 pages on money files record a step with no vote wording at all, such as a voice vote.
how: The shared reader of these roll calls takes a vote from the minutes only where the minutes name every member. The rows are the roll calls for which that failed, on money files and on lobbied measures, each with the reason. Where the minutes print an action twice, the tallies and the surnames voting no are given as the minutes print them. “What the counts use” is the final Board vote of the same file as counted on the other screens. The link opens the vote page, which names nobody.
limits: This is a gap in the published record, not in the votes, and nothing suggests the votes were unusual: 11 of the 17 are votes on an amendment or a continuance. The minutes print surnames; each was matched to the one member with that surname sitting at the time. The minutes read are the copies now linked from each meeting page. For 2 roll calls printed twice, the minutes also print a motion to rescind the previous vote on the same file; which of the two tallies the history row records is not stated. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
